thread:
elaine: Customer reporting sporadic 403s on /v1/generate. They say some requests work but others to the same project fail. Provided two x-request-ids and a curl.

sara: please paste both x-request-ids and the curl they ran so we can search logs.

elaine: request ids: req_20260320_a1b2c3, req_20260320_d4e5f6
curl they ran:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ABCD\" \\n  -H \"OpenAI-Organization: org-retail-99\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1.0\",\"input\":\"test\"}'
```
Response example:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: req_20260320_a1b2c3
{
  \"error\":\"access_denied\",
  \"message\":\"token lacks scope for project: proj-21\"
}
```

ravi: sounds like a token/project scope mismatch. Do we know which project the key is bound to?

devops: I'll look it up. elaine, confirm customer org and project values and whether they're using a service token or user key.

elaine: customer confirmed org: org-retail-99, project: proj-21. They rotated keys yesterday and found the token in their vault is issued to proj-9.

infra-bot: auth-lookup: req=req_20260320_a1b2c3 token_id=tok_svc_ab12 token_project=proj-9 effective_scopes=[generate:proj-9] target_org=org-retail-99 target_proj=proj-21 decision=DENY reason=scope_mismatch

sara: that matches the error. Recommend they either use a token scoped to proj-21 or drop the org header (if their default routing should use proj-9). Also ask them to verify token id in their vault and whether they accidentally rotated the wrong token.

ravi: also want to confirm our error message and logs are explicit enough without exposing secrets. Are we logging token ids and target proj? ok to include token_id but not token value.

devops: sanitized log line for req_20260320_a1b2c3:
```
[2026-03-20T15:12:07Z] req=req_20260320_a1b2c3 auth=tok_svc_ab12 token_proj=proj-9 target_org=org-retail-99 target_proj=proj-21 result=DENY reason=scope_mismatch
```
No secrets present.

elaine: asking customer to run a minimal repro curl and upload a debug bundle. Sending suggested curl now (masking token):
```
curl -i -v \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <THE_TOKEN>\" \\n  -H \"OpenAI-Organization: org-retail-99\" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1.0\",\"input\":\"repro: auth scope test\"}'
```
Ask them to paste full output including x-request-id and run `redwood debug bundle --request-id <x-request-id>` and share link.

sara: also ask them to try removing the `OpenAI-Organization` header as a quick check. If that flips to success, it's header-based routing. And ask for the exact timestamp of the failed calls.

devops: I'll enable a short-lived trace on auth service for token tok_svc_ab12 for 20 minutes. If they repro, send the new x-request-id and I'll attach the trace.

elaine: I will send the reply. Will include `vault read secret/service/proj-21` as a suggested check so they can confirm which token id they have in vault and whether it matches the one in logs.

sara: create a KB entry for \"403 caused by token scoped to wrong project/org header mismatch\" with sample log and repro steps.
